_comment: The DISCRIMINATION pilot declaration for skillc#287 (orchestrator review, comment 6025311708, decisions P1-P6). Exploratory only: estimates p_hat_intact and p_hat_degraded for evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's choose_n() - draws NO verdict (operator ruling, comment 6021089903).
_schema_note: This is deliberately NOT 'kind': 'calibration-declaration'. skillc.calibration.parse_declaration requires exactly one arm literally named 'baseline' whose subject is null (skillc/calibration.py: 'the baseline arm installs nothing: its subject is null'); it has no path for a 2-arm study where BOTH arms install a real subject, which is exactly the intact-vs-degraded contrast. A 3-arm declaration does not fit either - treated arms must declare an IDENTICAL subject, and a degraded arm's subject carries a 'degraded:...' revision label that is never identical to intact's. The orchestrator's accepted plan (comment 6025299008 section 5) calls this 'the existing matched-outcome shape, unmodified - no schema change', but the discrimination side of that plan cannot literally validate under skillc.calibration.parse_declaration as that function is written today - confirmed by reading it, not assumed. This is flagged to the orchestrator (mailbox, 2026-10-06) rather than resolved unilaterally, since calibration.py's arm-equality/baseline logic is adjacent to what claude-power-pack#1369's 61 golden cases pin and no schema change was approved. The resolution drafted here needs none: CPP#1084's own discrimination ruling (comment 6014163660, cited verbatim in skillc#287 comment 6014179807) says the test is counted 'over evaluable attempts from skillc's per-arm counts (#273's case-pairing facts)' - i.e. the discrimination accounting mechanism is skillc#273's case-pairing record (skillc/records.py: case_pairing(), TRIAL_LEDGER trials declaring case.arm in {intact, degraded} with a reciprocal case.paired_with), never skillc.calibration's declaration+Fisher pipeline. This file fixes n, tolerance, task and arm_order (the things ADR 0005 requires be fixed before any attempt) in the same vocabulary as a calibration-declaration for readability and cross-review, without claiming to be one.

pilot.purpose: exploratory - estimates p_hat_intact and p_hat_degraded for evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's choose_n(); draws no verdict
pilot.no_verdict_statement: This pilot draws no DISCRIMINATING / NOT_SHOWN / UNKNOWN verdict. Its 10 attempts per arm are too few to be the predeclared discrimination test itself (that test is the MAIN study's schedule, sized by this pilot's results) and are never pooled into the main study's counts (P1).
rule_citations: P1 (comment 6025311708): pilot attempts never count toward the main study.

P2 (comment 6025311708): the pilot uses the same two-declaration shape, one pilot declaration per test, each 2-arm at n=10, each separately approved at 10. The intact arm therefore runs in both pilot declarations (see pilot-improvement-declaration.json's 'intact' arm, same subject).

P3 (comment 6025311708): this pilot's own raw proportions (passes/evaluable) must never be plugged into the sizing simulation directly - convert with evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's jeffreys_estimate() first.
P5 (comment 6025311708): tolerance is max(1, ceil(0.05*n)) per arm, not a flat 1.

P6 (comment 6025311708): arm order is calibration's seed-derived interleaving, so the two arms run interleaved in time rather than as two blocks - skillc.calibration.derive_arm_order is reused here purely as a scheduling utility; this file is not parsed by skillc.calibration.parse_declaration (see _schema_note).

test: One-sided Fisher's exact test, H1: P(pass|intact) > P(pass|degraded), alpha 0.05, over evaluable attempts (claude-power-pack#1084 comment 6014163660, cited verbatim in skillc#287 comment 6014179807) - NOT run on this pilot's data (no_verdict_statement above); this field documents the MAIN study's test for cross-reference, since the pilot exists to size it.
